extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners, crisis-communication researchers, and social media managers
extracted.subtask_description: An honors thesis case study analyzing United Airlines Flight 3411 to evaluate crisis management and communication (using image repair theory) and to propose recommended organizational changes for future crises. Emphasis on the role of social media and the consequences of mixed messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy/strength of initial response
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the organization's response was substantive and appropriate versus 'lackluster responses' as described in the thesis abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page characterizes United's reaction as 'lackluster responses' — a strong rubric item is whether the organization issues clear, accountable, and forceful initial statements and actions that address harm and outline remediation steps. Anti-pattern: weak, defensive, or minimal statements that fail to acknowledge harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and cohesion of messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether communications were coherent and aligned across channels, avoiding 'mixed messaging' and the reported 'lack of a cohesive response.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract emphasizes 'mixed messaging' and 'lack of a cohesive response' as failures. Evaluation should check for unified talking points, internal coordination, and cross-channel consistency (press releases, social media, spokespeople). Anti-pattern: contradictory statements from different representatives or platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of response
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures how quickly the organization responded to the incident and ensuing public attention (videos went viral on Twitter), considering the time-sensitive nature of social-media-driven crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because passenger videos 'quickly went viral', an effective rubric includes responsiveness: fast acknowledgement, timely updates, and rapid engagement to reduce rumor and speculation. Anti-pattern: delayed responses that allow narratives to harden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of image repair strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the organization's communications align with established image repair theory principles (the thesis specifically analyzes 'image repair theory').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work 'explore[s] ... image repair theory' to examine where United's response failed; thus, criteria include use of denial, evasion, corrective action, mortification/apology, or other image-repair tactics appropriately and credibly. Scoring guidance: assess appropriateness and sincerity of chosen strategy and its fit for the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media and digital engagement management
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the organization's monitoring, engagement, and strategy on social platforms — the thesis analyzes 'the role of social media in crisis communication' and how 'digital engagement ... escalated the situation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric items: proactive monitoring, timely platform-specific responses, amplification control, engagement with affected parties, and mitigation of viral spread. Anti-patterns: ignoring social media, relying solely on traditional channels, or posting tone-deaf messages that fuel escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of failures and actionable recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the analysis identifies concrete failures in the response and proposes practical, implementable 'recommended changes the organization should make in future crisis response opportunities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis promises to 'propose recommended changes' — rubric should judge the specificity, feasibility, and strategic alignment of recommendations (e.g., policy changes, training, social-media protocols). High-quality recommendations are prioritized, evidence-based, and tied to observed failures.
